## Core Definitions

::: {.callout-tip}
### Memory Trick
* **I**ndependent = What **I** change or choose as the group/predictor.
* **D**ependent = The **D**ata **I** measure as the outcome.
:::

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🟢 Independent Variable
*(Explanatory / Input)*

* **What it is:** The variable that is changed, chosen, or used to divide data into groups.
* **Role:** The **cause** or **predictor**.
* **On a graph:** 
  * **X-axis** (horizontal)
  * **Group labels** on comparison plots
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🔵 Dependent Variable
*(Response / Outcome)*

* **What it is:** The variable being measured to see if it changes.
* **Role:** The **effect** or **outcome** (value *depends* on the independent variable).
* **On a graph:**
  * **Y-axis** (vertical)
  * **Numerical scale** on box/dot plots
:::

:::

---

## Variables in Year 11 Investigations

| Investigation Type | Independent Variable (Input / Group) | Dependent Variable (Measured Outcome) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Comparison** *(e.g., Foot length by Gender)* | **Categorical Group:** Gender *(Male vs. Female)* | **Numerical Response:** Foot length ($\text{mm}$) |
| **Relationship** *(e.g., Height vs. Arm Span)* | **Explanatory ($X$):** Height ($\text{cm}$) | **Response ($Y$):** Arm span ($\text{cm}$) |

---

## Mapping Variables to the PPDAC Cycle

::: {.callout-note}
### The PPDAC Enquiry Process

* **[ P ] Problem:** Define both variables clearly in your investigative question.  
  * *Example:* "I wonder if **Gender** (Independent) affects **Foot Length** (Dependent)?"
* **[ P ] Plan:** Decide how to group the Independent variable and measure the Dependent variable accurately without bias.
* **[ D ] Data:** Record data in paired structure: $(x, y) = (\text{Independent}, \text{Dependent})$.
* **[ A ] Analysis:** Plot Independent on X-axis and Dependent on Y-axis to compare distributions or trends.
* **[ C ] Conclusion:** Claim whether the Independent variable influences the Dependent variable in the wider population.
:::
